summary: Space-QHealth is a web app that works as an onboard medical control center for an astronaut crew. Astronauts check their own health through a crew dashboard with alerts and a clickable 3D body twin, and they get daily goals, explainable risk with recommendations, a fatigue test, a CPR emergency guide and messages to Earth. This lets them act on their own when help from the ground is delayed.
details:
Problem: on long missions the flight surgeon can be minutes away, and astronauts are not doctors.

What it does:

- Crew dashboard with an alert system and AI voice.

- Astronaut profile with a clickable 3D twin, daily goals and a clinical protocol.

- Module comparison across the crew, including Nutrition & Glucose with 30-day records, explainable risk, recommendations, an assistant and messages to Earth.

- Fatigue test (~1 min) combining PVT, Go/No-Go and Stroop tasks, after a simulated facial biometric check.

- CPR emergency guide with timer.

Data flow: live sensor readings streamed via SSE from a FastAPI backend, with fallback scenarios when the backend is unavailable. The face scan is simulated and nothing is sent.

Tech: React 19, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS v4, deployed on Vercel.

Not a medical device; values shown are simulated.
